title: Beyond the 956: Carlos Aleman, longtime Grupo Zereno frontman, dies at 63
excerpt: Carlos Aleman, the longtime lead vocalist of Grupo Zereno whose powerful voice helped define the Tejano sound for more than four decades, died November 12, 2026. He was 63.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Carlos Aleman, the longtime lead vocalist of Grupo Zereno whose powerful voice helped define the Tejano sound for more than four decades, has died at 63.

Aleman died Thursday, November 12, 2026, during a needed medical procedure after experiencing ongoing health issues, Tejano Nation reported. Grupo Zereno announced his death in a statement on social media.

“We are heartbroken as we share the sad news that our musical brother and front man for Zereno, Carlos Aleman, has gained his angel wings today November 12, 2026,” the group wrote. “Carlitos, we will miss you more than words can ever express. You were a true brother to us. We love you. Descansa en paz.”

Aleman began singing at a very young age alongside his father and went on to compete in singing competitions, including the prestigious OTI Festival, an international song competition showcasing vocal talent from across the Spanish-speaking world. After auditioning for Grupo Zereno, he impressed the band immediately and was chosen as its lead vocalist — a role he held for more than 40 years.

Formed in the mid-1980s in McAllen, Texas, Grupo Zereno became an established name in the Tejano music scene, with Aleman’s signature vocals at the forefront. His songs with the group included “Mi Amiga,” “Es Por Demás,” “Nació Un Amor,” “El Teléfono,” “Entiende Corazón” and the band’s signature song, “Hermoso Día.” Zereno recorded for National Records, Capitol EMI Latin and Fonovisa, and became known for its energetic live shows and its signature callout, “What time is it? Zereno Time!”

In October 2024, Aleman stepped away from Grupo Zereno after a 39-year run as its lead vocalist. By July 2025, he had officially reunited with the band, returning to the stage alongside longtime bandmates, including Jesse Cavazos and the San Roman brothers.

“Carlos had a very unique and powerful voice. He will be missed by his band mates, peers, his fans and especially his family,” longtime bandmate Mando San Roman said.

Rest in Peace, Carlos Aleman.

Sources: Tejano Nation; Grupo Zereno.
